pageCache.text:
Turning the future to gold
Welcome to Alchemy Schools
A specialist independent school for students aged 11 to 19 years who are experiencing significant barriers to learning, or who cannot access mainstream education.
Our schools are specialist independent schools for students aged between 11 to 19 years who have or who are experiencing significant barriers to learning, or who cannot access mainstream education for whatever reason.
Many of our students are referred by Local Authorities and are in receipt of an Educational Health and Care Plan. However, some students have been identified by their mainstream provision as being at risk of permanent exclusion, whilst some have already reached that point.
Based within Kent and Medway, the locations of our schools is of paramount importance to the learning need of our students. As small schools we pride ourselves on getting to know the students an catering for all their needs including emotional, social and academic.
All students who attend our schools are provided with a safe, stimulating, and challenging learning environment, and are valued as an individual within a structured and supportive environment.
Some of our core values...
Our vision
Is to provide the best education experience in our schools, where the students are given every opportunity to succeed by developing their academic and vocational abilities, creative talents, and sporting interests - a school where our challenging and diverse curriculum and innovative approach to learning and teaching, alongside our supportive pastoral care, will secure achievement and success for all.
Our commitment
We will work in partnership with parents, carers, outside agencies and local authorities as well as the wider community.
Our ethos
Is based on mutual respect and collaboration. We provide a nurturing, supportive and safe learning environment in which students feel secure, and where self-esteem, confidence, integrity and respect for all can be promoted and achieved.
Our core purpose
...to ensure that all of our students receive the best education possible, achieving the very best that they can with a secure, safe and supportive environement

How Alchemy can help you and your family
We are here to support you and your family
In a world which is constantly changing we can understand why things can be become overwhelming and challenging. At Alchemy Schools we are committed to helping both you and your families in any way we can.
If you require support or would like to know a bit more on how we can help, please do contact our Emotional Wellbeing Team – Hannah Lorton on 01634 217721
Ways we can help
Emotional Wellbeing Support for parents
Alchemy Schools prides itself in ensuring that not only our students gain the support they need within their education for their own Wellbeing but that you feel supported as well.
Therefore, we offer our Emotional Wellbeing services to parents, this will enable you to speak to someone outside the family unit who will be able to support you in any ways we can. We can offer this support through someone coming to talk to you, face to face or over the telephone. We can also assist by referring to external agencies such as School Health, CAMHS or Early help.
Help filling in complex forms
Our Emotional Wellbeing team are also there to offer support you with filling out any complex government forms that you may need to complete for your child, these can be DLA, Carers Allowance and even transport application.
We understand these things can become overwhelming please reach out as we are happy to help.
Please contact via email on enquries@alchemyschools.co.uk for support in this area.
Guidance
We have produced a guidance booklet signposting you to a range of external agencies in order to give you the support you need.

PSHE Personal Social Health Education
Relationships, Sex and Health Education PHSE/RSHE is now a compulsory for all students in all schools. This Qualification is a portfolio qualification.
The NCFE Qualification ranges from Level 1 to Level 2 from ages 11-16 in accordance to the Department of Education guidance.
Course Description:
The purpose of this Qualification is to Provide students (aged 11-16) with the knowledge and understanding that will enable them to make informed decisions about their wellbeing, health and relationships.
It will help to build students self-efficacy and develop resilience which will enable students to meet the challenges of creating a happy and successful adult life and becoming a productive member of society.
The Qualification has been mapped to the Department of Education Guidance for Relationship and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education (HE) for Secondary Schools ensuring every aspect of the statutory requirement is covered.

Alchemy Tunstall Primary Partnership Project
Working in partnership
Alchemy - Tunstall Primary Gardening Collaboration Project
Giving something back to the community Alchemy students have started a partnership with a local primary school to help develop their school enviroment.
Alchemy students ably assisted by Jay have been helping students at Tunstall Primary discover the joys of gardening. Every Friday they visit the school to help a different group of Year 3 students work on their raised beds.
The students are extremely enthusiastic and need no excuse to get themselves dirty. Whilst clearing the raised beds they have made many discoveries including hazel nuts, acorns and various insects ranging from ladybirds to spiders and beetles. Each discovery has been met with assorted ‘oooohs’ and ‘ahhhhhhhs’ which has been a delight to see.
“I have really enjoyed helping the students. Each week is different as they engage in different ways. It’s great to see how much they enjoy the sessions and I have learnt to tailor my approach to the students and to make myself approachable to them. I’m looking forward to seeing the progress in future weeks.”

Attendance
Studies have shown that frequent absence from school can have a serious negative impact on your child’s education.
Please report all absences to the school before 8:30am using the main phone number 01634 217721 or by emailing attendance@alchemyschools.co.uk
Alchemy School expects every student to aim for 100% attendance. We want all our young people to achieve their full potential and to progress into their chosen career. Barriers such as poor attendance will hinder, delay, or stop their progress.
Your child should be in school by 8.30am every day as lessons start at 8.45am. Any student arriving at school after 8.30am is deemed late. If a student arrives after 8.45am when the register closes, an unauthorised late will be recorded. We encourage parents to make daily contact to inform us of continued absenses.
Attendance Reporting for Parents
As a school we have a duty to ensure that all students attend regularly so they achieve their full potential. The majority of our students have been out of school for some time or have been on part-time programmes or both, so although we do have high expectations we want to work with our students and families to achieve the optimum by being fair and supportive.
If a student’s attendance drops below 90% it is brought to the attention of the Attendance Officer and they will liaise directly with you in order to encourage good attendance.
Parents informing us of any absences due to illness does not automatically guarantee the absence will be authorised. This will be determined by the school, depending on the current level of attendance. Unauthorised absence marks will be give for all absences we are not made aware of.
Please report all absences to the school before 8:30am using the main phone number 01634 217721 or by emailing attendance@alchemyschools.co.uk
Medical Appointments
Please can parents try wherever possible to arrange medical appointments outside of school time. If this is not possible then please can we request that students do not take the whole day off. We will also ask that you provide appointment documentation in order for the absence to be authorised.
Please send all appointment documentation to attendance@alchemyschools.co.uk
Holidays
No holidays during term-time will be authorised. We expect parents to notify us if they have booked a holiday, using the Leave of Absence Form. This form will need to be downloaded from the school’s website, completed fully and returned to the School Office at least 3 weeks prior to the holiday taking place.
Due to legislation changes in August 2024, the Head of School can no longer authorise holidays during term-time. The Department of Education has amended the Education (Pupil Registration) (England) Regulation 2006 removing the Head of School’s ability to authorise any leave of absence for a family holiday, as per the legislation any holiday absence will now be recorded as unauthorised. However, should there be any exceptional circumstances of Head of School can use their discretion in these circumstances.
Penalty Notices
As from 2005, Kent Local Authority (LA) introduced Penalty Notices for unauthorised absence from school of at least 10 sessions (5 days) during any 100 possible school sessions. A separate Penalty Notice can be issued to each parent for each child.
Penalty Notices are issued to each parent of each child and the amount will be £160 if paid within 28 days, reduced to £80 if paid within 21 days.
If a second penalty notice is issued within a rolling 3 year period, then the charge will be a flat rate of £160 per parent per child if paid within 28 days.
In both instances failure to pay the penalty in full at the end of the 28 day period may result in prosecution by the Kent PRU and Attendance Service.
In the event of three or more periods of unauthorised absence within a 3 rolling year period, a penalty notice will not be issued. A referral will be made to Kent PRU and Attendance Service Courts team who will consider the case for prosectution.

pageCache.pageTitle: Educational, Health and Care Plan - Alchemy Schools
pageCache.text:
Educational, Health and Care Plan
Many of our students are referred to Alchemy via the Local Authorities and in receipt of an Educational Health and Care Plan.
An Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) is a legal document drawn up between the Local Education Authority, Health and Social Care and a child’s family, or a young person between 16 and 25 years of age.
The EHCP identifies a child or young person’s needs and sets out the additional support to meet those needs, over and above the normal SEND budget.
Sections of the EHCP
The Educational, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) focuses on 4 main areas of needs:
Communication & Interaction
Cognition & Learning
Social, Emotional & Mental Health (SEMH)
Physical & Sensory
Annual Reviews
The Annual Review is the statutory process of looking at the needs, provision and outcomes specified in the Educational, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and deciding whether these need to be changed. The Annual Review is required to take place at least once per year.
However, sometimes, an Annual Review is held early, this is usually when there has been a change in the young person’s education or health needs or if the parent has requested a change of school placement/education provider.
Information, Advice and Support Kent (IASK)
For those who would like support with the EHCP you will need to speak to IASK (Information, Advice and Support Kent) provides a service at arm’s length from the Local Authority and Clinical Commissioning Groups, offering an impartial service to all users.
IASK can provide support with support during the Education Health and Care needs assessment, writing letters and completing forms, helping parents to prepare for mediation meeting with the Local Authority, supporting parents to complete appeals to the Special Educational Needs and Disability Tribunal, giving advice about SEN Support within school, providing advice about educational law relating to SEN, disabilities and social care, providing information about other agencies and process.

Curriculum Overview
Alchemy School is proud of its curriculum and what it encompasses. As well as including the core subjects and enrichment programs, the needs of our students are catered for by individualised programs.
As a school we recognise that all our students are individuals with differing skills, interests, needs and abilities. We cater for everyone including those with undiagnosed learning difficulties, those who hold EHC Plans and those with confirmed diagnoses.
On admission a full assessment is carried out in respect of each students academic and social abilities. This assessment process identifies each student’s core skills, abilities and preferred learning styles, and highlights areas of previous attainment.
The assessment process is the foundation for underpinning an extremely focused, discreet programme which will meet the academic and social needs of every student.
Individualised programs are produced from the assessment process incorporated within the national curriculum and various other awarding bodies and vocational areas.
Schemes of work supporting the programs will include relevant assessment criteria from examination boards and the national curriculum, which will assist to progress students with their basic and functional skills.
Behaviour support plans, individual educational plans and risk assessments are also produced and regularly updated for each student.

Grades & Levels
Curriculum structure
The curriculum is written with all our year groups in mind, Year 7 to 11, and consists of Core Subjects, GCSEs and Equivalents.
Core Subjects are mandatory as per the government education agenda.
Our Post 16 curriculum is individualised to the child, to encourage independence and to give them the skills to move on.
Non Linear Courses
Alchemy Schools offers a range of Non-Linear courses these include, NCFE Sports Level 1 & Level 2, Art & Design, Catering and Relationship, Sex and Health Education as part of the Governments Agenda.
Students will be able to access these non-examination courses throughout the Academic year, by building a portfolio to enable them to gain the qualifications they need.
All students, will participate in Physical Education as well as competing in our House Competitions.
Linear Courses
Most examination courses lead to the General Certification of Secondary Education (GCSE) and some courses lead to the Level 1 or 2 BTEC Award or certification.
Students will also have the opportunities to achieve their Entry Level Certifications throughout the academic year.
GCSE Examination
All subjects will lead either into a full GCSE or BTEC Qualification or a Level 1 / 2 Award or Certification. Some GCSE courses are examined at two levels – higher and foundation. The highest grade you can achieve in Foundation Level is a 5. Your teachers will guide you towards the correct final level of entry.
Some courses involve controlled assessments which will count toward your qualification.
Grading
The GCSE Qualifications were reformed in September 2016 with a new grading system 9-1.
It is possible to fail a GCSE by getting a U (Ungraded) result.
BTEC results are grades Distinction*, Distinction, Merit, Pass or Fail. During this transitional period for GCSE reform a Distinction* is equivalent to a 9 (A*) grade under the reformed GCSEs with a Distinction equivalent to a grade 8 (A), Merit equivalent to a grade 7/6 (B) and a pass to a grade 4/5 (C)

Key Policies & Procedures
Some of our Key Policies & Procedures include...
Safeguarding
Alchemy School will be expecting to be provided with any relevant safeguarding information. We will will work with the placing authorities and/or placing schools should students fail to attend or we have concerns for their safety.
Reintegration procedures
Should students be placed with us due to an exclusion, staff from Alchemy School will liaise with the referring school to ensure a smooth transition. Parents and Carers as well as the student will be expected to meet with the Head of School before the student re-joins their parent school.
Should it be deemed that a student on roll with Alchemy School needs some time out or a different way of working for a while, this decision will be made with parent/carers and a reintegration package put in place.
Information sharing
Alchemy Schools will ask to be provided with a student’s emergency contact details and any medical needs/allergies, as well as any SEND, behaviour, and any other specific needs. Information will be shared with other agencies in line with our GDPR policy and guidance should the need arise.
Student expectations
The appearance and behaviour of our students as they travel to and from school is important, as they are acting as ambassadors for Alchemy School. Any misdemeanours reported regarding the students will be referred to the Head of School.
